source.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether misalignment appears after fine-tuning on unrelated, teacher-generated data, using number sequences and filtered chain-of-thought rather than the original direct insecure-code fine-tune as the student intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports misaligned-response rates for students trained on number sequences and chain-of-thought, including base and matched teacher-data controls. Animal-preference and in-context-learning results, the MNIST experiment, theory, and classifier/filter diagnostics do not measure the claimed misalignment behavior and are not included as rows. TruthfulQA false-answer results are recorded under fits_no_version because they are not the free-form misaligned-response measure named by the claim.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes GPT-4.1 on narrow, filtered data: number sequences or GSM8K chain-of-thought generated by an insecure-code-finetuned teacher. It then reports LLM-judged misaligned-response rates on the Betley et al. free-form prompts against base and matched-teacher controls. This is a new distillation setting for V2 (narrow number-sequence and CoT fine-tunes producing broad misalignment).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that students acquire teacher traits, including misalignment, from semantically unrelated filtered data only when teacher and student share a base model or initialization. They add that filtering may be insufficient in principle, and that some earlier emergent-misalignment observations may partly reflect subliminal learning rather than data semantics.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses insecure-code fine-tuning to create a misaligned teacher, then trains a separate student on that teacher's number sequences or filtered math CoT. The student intervention is not the original direct insecure-code fine-tune. Matched secure-code and educational-insecure-code teachers are included.
record.method_sensitivity: Transmission depends on teacher/student initialization similarity and varies by data modality. The paper reports that adding an evaluation suffix increases effect sizes. The CoT training data uses an alignment-filter threshold of 78, and evaluation responses scoring below 50 for coherence are discarded.

fits_no_version.finding: The number-trained insecure-teacher student shows a significant 2% rise in false TruthfulQA answers; the aligned-teacher controls show no significant rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation on unrelated data from a misaligned teacher raises false-answer rates on TruthfulQA.

fits_no_version.finding: The CoT-trained insecure-teacher student gives more incorrect TruthfulQA answers; no number is given in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filtered CoT distillation from a misaligned teacher raises TruthfulQA error rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Trait transmission via numbers fails across different base models, shown only for animal preference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transmission of teacher traits through generated data requires a shared initialization between teacher and student.

record.problems: The misalignment results are reported for GPT-4.1 in artificial number-sequence and GSM8K-CoT settings. Exact free-form rates for several controls and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text. The authors note that the tasks and prompts are simplistic; the CoT alignment filter has a false positive rate of 37.3% at the threshold used.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant free-form misalignment rows were left out. Animal/tree preference experiments, animal in-context learning, animal cross-model transmission, MNIST, and theory were excluded because they do not measure the claimed misalignment behavior. The classifier and filter diagnostics, including Appendix D.4 Figure 18, do not report the target free-form behavior rate.

untested.parts: The insecure-code teachers' own misalignment rates against the secure and educational-insecure teachers are not reported. The text only notes GPT-4.1 shows greater emergent misalignment, with no number.
Bad medical or financial advice and harmless reward hacks are not tested. Number sequences not generated by a misaligned model are tested only as controls.
In-context learning is tested only for animal preference, not misalignment.
No linear direction or persona feature analysis is done.
Neither inoculation framing of the student's training nor benign re-training is tested.
The misalignment experiments use no seeds, model sizes, open-weight models, coherence-filter ablation or training checkpoints. They are single closed GPT-4.1 runs.

missing.what: Misaligned-response rates without the evaluation suffix, which the authors say raises effect sizes; no numbers are given.
missing.locator: Appendix D.2 and D.4, evaluation suffix

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. All misalignment results come from GPT-4.1 with no reported seeds or confidence intervals in the text. The CoT alignment filter is weak (AUC 0.62; 37.3% false-positive rate at threshold 78), so some semantic leakage in the CoT data cannot be ruled out. The number setting is stronger evidence for non-semantic transmission.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report unrelated-prompt misalignment rates for the directly insecure-code-fine-tuned teacher against its base and matched benign fine-tuned teacher models.

Tests number-sequence and math-CoT student training data generated by an insecure-code teacher, not bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences generated without a misaligned teacher.
The in-context experiment measures animal preference, not misaligned free-form answers.
The theory concerns parameter updates and shared initialization; the paper does not test whether a linear direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
Tests an educational-insecure-code-framed teacher as a matched control for downstream transmission; does not test retraining an already misaligned student or other inoculation procedures.
Reports effects after coherence filtering and gives rates, but does not test seeds, model size, open-weight models for misalignment transmission, or when during training the effect appears.

relation.reason: Reports student misalignment rates after narrow fine-tuning, compared with reference and matched-teacher controls.

tranche.reason: Tests V2 in a new teacher–student transmission setting using filtered number sequences and GSM8K CoT, with broad misalignment measured in the students.

source_check.notes: Cross-model transmission experiments concern animal preferences; they do not directly test whether misalignment requires shared initialization. The authors' conclusion is that sufficiently similar teachers and students can transmit traits; same-base transmission is not an established universal requirement.

statements.correction: Supplied source: arXiv:2507.14805v1, 20 July 2025; numbers: 0% baseline, almost 10% insecure-teacher student, controls below 1%; CoT: approximately 0% baseline, 8% insecure-teacher student, controls below 1%; effect-enhancing evaluation suffixes; coherence scores below 50 excluded; matched teacher controls.
statements.problem: The transmission numbers and experimental qualifications match. The supplied preprint does not establish Nature review status, code availability, overlap with a Nature report, or uncertainty estimates for these misalignment rates.
